The vision

What if carbon had
a different next chapter?

CO₂ is a climate challenge. Carbon is also a building block for valuable materials. OxyGen brings these two perspectives together.

Our ambition is to explore a pathway from captured atmospheric CO₂ to useful solid carbon materials, with oxygen as a potential co-product. We’re investigating how carbon capture and utilisation could work together in one system.

A research direction, with work ahead. Our proposed system is still in development; its performance and environmental impact require experimental validation.

THE RESEARCH QUESTION / 01

How can the air become a starting point?

We’re exploring how atmospheric CO₂ could supply a materials-focused system. Capture efficiency and resource requirements are questions to evaluate.

Explore a collaboration ↗
Where we are

Big questions.
Practical next steps.

OxyGen is an early-stage project moving toward experimental proof of concept. Our focus is on testing the science, understanding the engineering, and learning what a useful system would need to deliver.

Is OxyGen commercially available?

Not yet. We are in the research and development stage, before a working prototype. This website introduces our direction rather than an available product.

What kind of collaboration are you looking for?

We welcome conversations with researchers, laboratories, materials specialists, and people working in carbon capture and utilisation.

Does this mean permanent carbon removal?

That cannot be assumed. Climate impact depends on the full lifecycle, energy inputs, material use and end of life. These questions need evidence as the project develops.

Development snapshot

Research first.
Evidence next.

We’re building a foundation for experimental work, with the aim of turning a proposed pathway into measurable results.

  • Current stage: concept development
  • Current focus: proof-of-concept planning
  • Next milestone: experimental validation
The people behind the idea

Two founders.
One question worth pursuing.

Could the carbon we capture from the air become the starting point for something useful?

That question is at the heart of OxyGen. We’re Max and Nika, and we’re building an early-stage venture around atmospheric carbon and materials research.

Our next step is practical: move toward experimental proof of concept, test the proposed pathway, and learn from the results. We’re looking to connect with people who can help us take that step.
